details:
The Kerala Disaster Relief System is a proposed data-driven solution for supporting disaster management in Kerala. The main aim is to help identify disaster-affected areas and support better planning during emergencies.

The proposed system brings together different types of information, including weather reports, rainfall records, satellite observations, population statistics, geographical maps, and historical disaster data. These data sources can help users understand disaster situations and identify areas that may need attention.

The system is designed to present important information in an organised way and support decision-making during disaster response. Its intended benefits include better emergency planning, improved awareness of affected areas, and more effective allocation of relief resources.

Our project focuses on using data and technology to address disaster-management challenges in Kerala.
